newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-BHP,Japan reach agreement on iron ore.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-BHP,Japan reach agreement on iron ore.

text.p: The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd said on Tuesday it has won a 1.1 percent price rise from Japanese steel mills for 1997/98 (April-March) deliveries of Mount Newman fines iron ore.
BHP said it agreed to a price of 29.10 U.S. cents per dry long ton unit for fines.
The 1997/98 price for Mount Newman lump ore was unchanged from the previous year at 37.68 U.S. cents a dry long ton, BHP said.
Delivery tonnages for Mount Newman ore to the Japanese mills in 1997/98 had been agreed at 14.6 million tons, the same level as agreed for the previous year, BHP said.
BHP Iron Ore Group General Manager Geoff Wedlock said BHP believed the outcome was realistic in the current business climate.

"The settlement reflects the uncertain economic conditions in Japan and the prospects for the Japanese Steel Mills, while acknowledging the current iron ore market circumstances and future iron ore supply," Wedlock said in a statement.
"The settlement also demonstrates the mature long term relationship with our customers in Japan, which has enabled this agreement to be reached in a complex market situation.
"Economic conditions remain flat, with industry predictions that annual crude steel production in Japan is likely to contract by one million tonnes next year to about 98 million tonnes," he said.
Agreements for prices for other BHP iron ore products had not yet been completed but would follow shortly.
The differential between lump and fines reflected a slight easing of the relative attractiveness of lump ore over the past 12 months.
Analysts said the modest gain in the price for fines represented a slight coup for BHP and other Australian preoducers, given expectations of declining steel production.
Australia's second largest iron ore miner, the Hamersley iron division of RTZ-CRA, and other producers had not yet released terms for 1997/98.
